turn_text: Hey, it's great to be with you and your listeners.

I want to begin with questions that I know are of importance to you and I'll follow up the first specific question with a couple of local aspects of that. I'd like to know how you and other legislators respond to these trends.

Well I think what this has forced us to do is to get even more proactive about speaking out about our public lands in our state about really getting focused on the special places that deserve additional layers of protection and to do the kind of homework that it requires to put a community-based coalition together and to develop plans to protect those special places. And if there is a silver lining to the hostility that the Trump administration has brought to resources, to outdoor resources, then our environment generally, it's that I think it is forcing many communities to think about what's really near and dear to them and how they're going to work to protect those resources long-term.

I'm hearing in what you said that this depends on us, the constituents, and not only on you, the legislators, and that relates directly to my next question, Senator Heinrich. There is so much concern in our region about a possible diversion of the free-flowing Hilo River. Do you support protection of the Hilo River by designating it as a wild and scenic river with unique special qualities?

So let's unpack that a little bit. I think first I want to say that I don't think that it is appropriate to dam or divert the Gila. I think that's a half baked idea that would spend an awful lot of money and not result in a lot of water at the end of the day. And it could mar one of the great, you know, one of the last free flowing rivers in the West. And I think that the HILA has incredible values. There is an active coalition working on looking at the HILA and coming up with citizen-based proposals for what might be designated under Wild and Scenic. fan of the Hila River. I think it's a great one of the great resources in southwestern New Mexico. The whole community has an awful lot of pride in it. And we look forward to hearing from everyone about how they believe that we should protect this resource.
